236.canonical: Close a session or retrieval guide with a brief closed-resource prompt for a salient takeaway, use the responses as formative evidence, review them before the next meeting, and open by addressing the common errors or uncertainties they reveal.

241.canonical: Keep cumulative assessment sustainable by maintaining a reusable pool of essential earlier questions, sampling from it rather than testing everything, and pruning it around enduring themes, essential questions, and future performance needs when it becomes unwieldy.

251.canonical: Before revealing an answer, have learners judge their own knowledge state — known, once known, or never learned — then check that judgment by retrieving predicted-known items without resources, looking up the uncertain ones, and verifying every generated answer against feedback.

257.canonical: Audit a learning tool or combined design by its mechanisms — retrieval format, timing, stakes, spacing, interleaving, discrimination demand, mastery controls, feedback quality, visible progress data, and the evidence behind its claims — rather than by the presence of several named techniques.

262.canonical: Offer the same repertoire of evidence-aligned retrieval and feedback routines across learner groups, determining individual modifications collaboratively from observed outcomes rather than by categorical exclusion, uniform implementation, or learner preference.
